dates.note: The list entry says '1723-29 Architect Nicholas Hawksmoor'. The Wikipedia infobox for the same building prints 'Consecrated July 1729' and gives the build as 1714-1729. Both are recorded and neither is resolved.

quotes.text: 1723-29 Architect Nicholas Hawksmoor. White ashlar tower and spire dominate the Spitalfields area. Western portico of 4 giant Tuscan columns. Central semi-circular arch, a theme repeated in the facade below tower. Steps. Interior (apart from crypt) now closed for restoration.

note: Tranche 3, English Baroque / Palladian / Adam cluster, 5 Sep 2026. A CHURCH, AND IT IS HERE BECAUSE THIS NODE'S OWN PROSE MAKES THE CITY CHURCHES THE STYLE'S ORIGIN; that placement is editorial and the register does not make it. TWO WORDS ABOUT WHAT A LEGACY LIST ENTRY IS WORTH: its whole description is six short sentences for one of the three or four most-discussed buildings of the English Baroque -- re-counted against the page on 5 Sep 2026, where an earlier reading of this record said four -- and its last sentence -- 'Interior (apart from crypt) now closed for restoration' -- has been out of date since services returned in 1987. A list entry states a condition as of the year it was written, and nothing on the page says which year that description is from. Historic England serves the Details section hard-wrapped. Every run of whitespace in these quotes is the extractor's line wrap collapsed to one space; nothing else was changed, and a word broken across a wrap is left broken. No rights line for the list entry TEXT was returned by any extract of THIS entry, so no `rights_evidence` is recorded rather than one borrowed from a sibling entry; Historic England does print one in the footer of the official-list-entry view, read verbatim on 5 Sep 2026 on entry 1253989 and recorded there.
